title: Proprietary and Fiduciary Funds
html:
Proprietary Funds

Proprietary Funds

Proprietary funds account for government activities that operate in a manner similar to commercial businesses.

Unlike governmental funds, proprietary funds use:

ECONOMIC RESOURCES MEASUREMENT FOCUS + ACCRUAL BASIS OF ACCOUNTING

This means proprietary funds generally recognize assets, liabilities, revenues, and expenses similarly to business enterprises.

Two Types of Proprietary Funds

Enterprise Fund Provides Goods or Services Primarily to External Users
Internal Service Fund Provides Goods or Services Primarily to Other Government Departments

Enterprise Funds

Enterprise funds generally account for activities in which goods or services are provided to the public or other external users for a fee.

Enterprise fund reporting may also be required when applicable criteria are met, such as when laws, regulations, debt arrangements, or pricing policies require an activity's costs to be recovered primarily through fees and charges.

Common Examples
  • Public water utilities
  • Government-owned airports
  • Public transit systems
  • Government parking operations

Think:

Government + customers outside the government + user charges → Enterprise Fund.

Internal Service Funds

Internal service funds generally account for goods or services provided by one department or agency of a government to other departments or agencies, usually on a cost-reimbursement basis.

Example

A city's centralized motor pool maintains vehicles for the police, fire, and parks departments and charges those departments for the services.

The activity may be accounted for in an internal service fund.

EXTERNAL CUSTOMERS → ENTERPRISE INTERNAL DEPARTMENTS → INTERNAL SERVICE

Capital Assets

Because proprietary funds use the economic resources measurement focus, they generally report capital assets directly in the fund.

Capital assets are also generally depreciated.

Equipment Cost $300,000
Useful Life 10 Years
$300,000 ÷ 10 = $30,000 Annual Depreciation

This is very different from a governmental fund, where acquisition of equipment is generally reported as an expenditure rather than recording and depreciating the capital asset in the fund.

Long-Term Debt

Proprietary funds generally report their long-term liabilities directly because they use the economic resources measurement focus.

PROPRIETARY FUND Capital Assets ✓ Depreciation ✓ Long-Term Liabilities ✓

Revenues and Expenses

Proprietary fund statements distinguish operating activities from nonoperating activities.

Operating Examples

  • Charges to customers for services
  • Employee costs related to operations
  • Supplies and other operating costs

Nonoperating Examples

  • Interest revenue
  • Interest expense
  • Certain investment-related amounts

Proprietary Fund Statements

Proprietary funds generally present:

Statement of Net Position Financial Position
Statement of Revenues, Expenses, and Changes in Fund Net Position Operating Results
Statement of Cash Flows Cash Activity

Important Cash Flow Difference

Proprietary fund cash flow statements use categories that differ somewhat from those commonly seen in business accounting.

One important CPA distinction is that proprietary fund statements include an operating activities category based on governmental reporting requirements, along with noncapital financing, capital and related financing, and investing activities.

Governmental vs. Proprietary

Governmental Funds Modified Accrual + Current Financial Resources
Proprietary Funds Accrual + Economic Resources

CPA Memory Rule

ENTERPRISE = OUTSIDE USERS INTERNAL SERVICE = INSIDE USERS BOTH = ACCRUAL + ECONOMIC RESOURCES

Key Takeaways

  • Proprietary funds use accrual accounting.
  • They use the economic resources measurement focus.
  • Enterprise funds generally serve external users.
  • Internal service funds generally serve other government departments.
  • Proprietary funds report and depreciate capital assets.
  • They generally report their long-term liabilities directly.

Fiduciary Funds

Fiduciary Funds

Fiduciary funds account for resources that a government holds or administers in a fiduciary capacity for others.

The key idea is that these resources generally are not available to support the government's own programs.

FIDUCIARY FUNDS = RESOURCES HELD FOR OTHERS + ECONOMIC RESOURCES + ACCRUAL BASIS

Four Fiduciary Fund Types

Pension and Other Employee Benefit Trust Funds Employee Benefit Arrangements
Investment Trust Funds External Portion of Investment Pools
Private-Purpose Trust Funds Trusts Benefiting Specific Individuals or Organizations
Custodial Funds Fiduciary Resources Not Reported in Another Fiduciary Fund

Pension and Other Employee Benefit Trust Funds

These funds account for qualifying pension plans and other employee benefit arrangements administered through a trust or equivalent arrangement.

Example

A city administers a pension trust for retired municipal employees.

The pension resources belong to the plan's participants and beneficiaries rather than being available for ordinary city programs.

Investment Trust Funds

Investment trust funds generally report the external portion of investment pools administered by a sponsoring government.

Example

A county manages an investment pool containing its own money as well as money belonging to legally separate local governments.

The qualifying external portion may be reported in an investment trust fund.

Private-Purpose Trust Funds

Private-purpose trust funds account for certain fiduciary activities held in trust for the benefit of specific individuals, private organizations, or other governments.

The beneficiaries are not the government's own programs or the public generally.

Custodial Funds

Custodial funds account for qualifying fiduciary activities that are not required to be reported in one of the three trust fund categories.

Example

A government collects certain amounts on behalf of another government and later remits those resources to that government.

Fiduciary Funds and Government-Wide Statements

This is an important CPA distinction:

FIDUCIARY ACTIVITIES ARE GENERALLY EXCLUDED FROM GOVERNMENT-WIDE FINANCIAL STATEMENTS

Why?

Because fiduciary resources generally cannot be used to support the government's own programs and activities.

Basis of Accounting

Fiduciary funds use the economic resources measurement focus and the accrual basis of accounting.

Governmental Funds Modified Accrual
Proprietary Funds Accrual
Fiduciary Funds Accrual

Fiduciary Financial Statements

Fiduciary funds generally report:

  • Statement of Fiduciary Net Position
  • Statement of Changes in Fiduciary Net Position

Don't Confuse Permanent and Private-Purpose Trust Funds

This distinction is especially useful for FAR.

Permanent Fund Benefits Government or Its Citizenry
Private-Purpose Trust Fund Benefits Specific Outside Individuals or Organizations
BENEFITS GOVERNMENT / CITIZENS → PERMANENT FUND BENEFITS SPECIFIC OUTSIDERS → PRIVATE-PURPOSE TRUST

CPA Memory Rule

  • Fiduciary = government holds resources for others.
  • Fiduciary funds use accrual accounting.
  • They use the economic resources measurement focus.
  • Fiduciary activities are generally excluded from government-wide statements.
  • Remember the four types: pension/employee benefit trust, investment trust, private-purpose trust, and custodial.

Key Takeaway

When a CPA question says the government is holding or administering resources for someone else, consider whether fiduciary fund reporting applies.

quiz.prompt: A city-owned water utility primarily provides services to residents for a fee. Which fund is generally appropriate?
quiz.explanation: Enterprise funds generally report activities that provide goods or services primarily to external users for a fee.
